title.narrative: Provision of life-saving assistance to the affected population due to Cyclone Chido through Shelter/NFI and CCCM in Mozambique

description.narrative: Tropical Cyclone Chido, a Category 4 storm, made landfall in northern Mozambique on 15 December 2024, impacting Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa provinces. The cyclone brought torrential rains of 250 mm within 24 hours, accompanied by wind gusts reaching up to 260 km/h. According to data collected by IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) and validated by the National Institute for Natural Disaster Management (INGD), a total of 321,150 people were estimated to have been impacted by the cyclone, with 45 people dead and 493 injured. More than 21,113 houses were completely or partially destroyed, and 78 schools, 9 health units, and 19 administrative blocks were damaged. These figures have been increasing as more assessments are conducted.Shelter, food, and non-food items (NFIs) remain the most urgent needs for the affected population, along with coordinated support in displacement sites and accommodation centers. Joint multi-sectoral needs assessments, led by INGD and humanitarian partners, are ongoing. Through the CERF allocation, IOM aims to provide life-saving assistance to populations affected by Cyclone Chido by addressing urgent needs for shelter and non-food items while ensuring effective coordination and management of displacement sites through the implementation of Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) activities.By delivering CCCM services to an estimated 108,500 individuals whose accommodations have been fully destroyed, IOM will enable access to vital information on available services and assistance. Through referrals, service coordination, and site improvements, IOM will enhance the safety, dignity, and overall living conditions within displacement sites and accommodation centers. Communities will be at the center of all activities, with ongoing consultations and effective community feedback mechanisms to ensure their needs and voices are integrated.
